attempts.summary: Configured node1 to mirror the traffic it exchanges with node2 on the shared 'seg' L2 segment to node3, using a GRETAP tunnel from node1 to node3 combined with tc/flower filters (ingress and egress, matched on node2's IP, plus ARP) that mirror matching frames into the tunnel. node3 decapsulates via a matching gretap interface (mirr0) and a capture there shows the original node1<->node2 packets, still addressed to each other and not to node3. node1<->node2 traffic itself continues unaffected (verified 0% ping loss throughout, before and after all restarts). Configuration was made persistent via systemd oneshot services on node1 and node3, and static seg-network IPs were made persistent (ifupdown on node1, NetworkManager on node2/node3). All three nodes were restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot IDs were proven to change on each restart, and after each restart the mirror setup was verified to recover (a bug in the persistence script's qdisc-existence check surfaced after node1's first restart, was fixed, and re-verified working end-to-end; node3's restart later exercised the corrected script cleanly on first try).
